title: Genome-wide SNP analysis reveals genetic diversity and population structure in Ethiopian naked barley (Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum)
content:
by Tesfaye Woldesemayate Woldetsadik, Tileye Feyissa, Tilahun Mekonnen, Alemayehu Teressa Negawo, Basazen Fantahun Lakew

Ethiopian naked barley (Hordeum vulgare L. var. nudum) represents a vital traditional cereal crop adapted to diverse and challenging highland agroecologies. Despite its agronomic and nutritional significance, high-density, genome-wide genetic characterization of this germ plasm remains limited. Therefore, the objective of this study was to investigate the genetic diversity, population structure, admixture patterns, and genomic differentiation of Ethiopian naked barley accessions. We used 222 lines and 8,072 high-quality single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers spanning chromosomes 1H–7H and unanchored genomic regions. Diversity parameters, including minor allele frequency (MAF), expected heterozygosity (He), and polymorphic information content (PIC), were evaluated. Population structure was resolved via a multi-method consensus framework incorporating sNMF ancestry analysis (LEA), Discriminant Analysis of Principal Components (DAPC), identity-by-state (IBS) hierarchical clustering, Principal Coordinate Analysis (PCoA), and neighbor-joining clustering. Spatial and population-level differentiation were quantified using pairwise fixation indices (FST), analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA), and Mantel isolation-by-distance tests. Genome-wide SNP diversity was moderate (MAF = 0.214; He = 0.292; PIC = 0.236), whereas population-level diversity varied across the six geographic populations (He = 0.204–0.273; Ho = 0.029–0.036; FIS = 0.805–0.847), indicating substantial within-population structure. Structural analyses consistently identified K = 8 as the optimal genetic cluster model, revealing distinct population stratification accompanied by varying degrees of admixture. While several accessions exhibited strong lineage assignment to specific clusters, others displayed highly mixed ancestry, indicating historical gene flow and incomplete isolation. Pairwise FST estimates and AMOVA confirmed significant, moderate genetic differentiation among geographic populations (P < 0.001). These findings demonstrate that Ethiopian naked barley germ plasm harbors substantial structured genetic diversity despite the high lineage fixation typical of autogamous species. The sub populations and admixed lines identified herein provide useful resources for future allele mining, association mapping, and climate-resilient, nutritionally enhanced breeding programs.
